Denise / Sara,

Thanks — excited to move this forward. High level answers below; attaching a short capability matrix and a draft MAP to speed the procurement conversation. Full tech deep-dive would be best on a call (Karthik will run the technical sync).

- Metering: Redwood supports both push-based and pull-based metering. We can call the AWS SaaS Metering API directly from our backend (recommended when the customer instance is managed by us) or send signed usage webhooks to the AWS fulfillment endpoint. We support SKU-level and customer-id mapping; seat-based mappings are supported via a lightweight proxy layer if the customer tracks seats separately.
- Fulfillment: we prefer to offer two modes — (A) AWS-managed entitlements (SaaS Fulfillment) where AWS issues entitlements and we validate via APIs, or (B) Redwood-managed entitlements where we handle access and report usage for billing. For co-sell customers who want AWS-managed procurement, we usually recommend (A) for smoother marketplace invoicing.
- Billing reconciliation: standard playbook is 30 day reconcile window, invoice matching by SKU and customer-id, and a two-week dispute resolution SLA for usage claims. If Acme needs tighter windows, Naomi can comment on contract language.

Soojin / Denise / Sara — taking the technical thread. Short tech notes and gotchas from our engineering side: 

1) Metering modes we support:
   - Direct SaaS Metering API call: Redwood can emit MeterUsage calls to AWS using the customer/aws-account mapping. Good when we host the tenant and control usage emission timing.
   - Webhook push to AWS: Redwood can sign and POST compressed usage batches. This is preferable if the customer wants to retain full usage records and host an ingestion endpoint.

2) Entitlement mapping:
   - Preferred: 1:1 SKU mapping (Redwood SKU -> AWS Marketplace SKU). This keeps reconciliation simple.
   - Alternative: composite mappings (model_variant+context) that resolve on our side to a single marketplace SKU for billing. We'll provide a JSON mapping table during the tech call.

3) Reconciliation & idempotency:
   - Our events include idempotency keys and per-interval checksums. We can re-run historical exports for backfills (important for migration customers).

4) Multi-cloud (GCP) considerations:
   - GCP marketplace uses a different entitlement flow; if Acme wants a single purchase experience across clouds, we recommend: route procurement through AWS for co-sell + implement a compatibility adapter for GCP (same internal SKU -> different marketplace token exchange). This adapter adds ~2-3 engineering weeks for CI and E2E tests.

5) Security & audit: we support signed JWT for webhook auth, and can integrate with customer KMS for payload encryption on request.

Attachments: sample-sow-aws-saas.docx (draft SOW with metering clauses)

I can demo the MeterUsage sequence and a small replay tool in the tech sync. Proposed agenda: meter emission flow, entitlement mapping JSON, backfill process, test accounts & signing keys.

Thanks team — quick procurement & finance notes from Redwood's side: 

- Contracting route: for AWS-managed procurement we typically attach an Appendix A that states the reconciliation cadence, data fields required for invoice matching, and the dispute SLA (two-week review). Please note our standard commercial asks: 30 day payment terms, clear limitation of liability carveouts for marketplace-billed items, and support for invoice-level credits.
- SOW language: prefer a clause that allows Redwood to export a usage report for both parties and to support a backfill reconciliation if discrepancies exceed 2% in a billing period. We're okay with AWS-managed entitlements as long as we retain read-only entitlement verification APIs.
- Audit evidence: the marketplace team will request sample logs; we'll provide a redacted export for Acme during the enablement if requested.

Action items for this thread: Naomi -> draft appendix and sample SOW (I will use the attached draft as a starting point), Marissa -> confirm DocuSign path and whether Acme requires a third-party master agreement on top of AWS purchase.
